record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What asymptotic conditions allow the conformal method to construct Einstein initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold, such as a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface meeting future null infinity, thereby producing hyperboloidal initial data?

evidence.quote: construct initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g, K)$ be an initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $M$ is a smooth $3$-manifold, $g$ a Riemannian metric on $M$, and $K$ a symmetric $2$-tensor satisfying the Einstein constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0.$$
Suppose $M$ is the interior of a compact manifold-with-boundary $\overline{M}$ whose boundary $\partial M$ represents future null infinity, and that $(M,g)$ is asymptotically hyperbolic in the sense that there exists a defining function $\rho$ for $\partial M$ and a smooth metric $\bar g = \rho^2 g$ on $\overline{M}$ with $|d\rho|_{\bar g} = 1$ on $\partial M$. Suppose further that $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ is constant on $M$ (a CMC slice), modeling a hyperboloidal hypersurface meeting future null infinity transversally.

In the conformal method one prescribes a conformal background $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ — where $\tilde g$ is a Riemannian metric on $M$, $\sigma$ a transverse-traceless symmetric $2$-tensor with respect to $\tilde g$, and $\tau$ the prescribed mean curvature — and seeks a positive conformal factor $\phi$ and a vector field $W$ such that
$$g = \phi^4 \tilde g, \qquad K = \phi^{-2}(\sigma + \mathcal{L}_{\tilde g} W) + \tfrac{\tau}{3}\, g,$$
solve the constraint equations, where $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde g}$ denotes the conformal Killing operator of $\tilde g$. This reduces the constraints to the coupled Lichnerowicz–vector equations for $(\phi, W)$ on $M$.

Problem. Determine the precise asymptotic conditions on the conformal data $(\tilde g, \sigma, \tau)$ at $\partial M$ — including the rates of decay or polyhomogeneous expansion of $\tilde g - \bar g$, $\sigma$, and $\tau - \tau_\infty$ near $\rho = 0$, as well as compatibility/boundary conditions at $\partial M$ — under which the conformal method produces a solution $(\phi, W)$ giving a vacuum hyperboloidal initial data set $(M, g, K)$ that is asymptotically hyperbolic with the prescribed asymptotic geometry, with $\mathrm{tr}_g K$ constant, and such that $\partial M$ corresponds to future null infinity of the resulting maximal Cauchy development.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial partial results exist: Andersson–Chruściel–Friedrich and subsequent work established existence of CMC hyperboloidal solutions of the conformal constraints under suitable asymptotic conditions, while showing that generic solutions admit only polyhomogeneous (logarithmic) expansions at conformal infinity rather than smooth ones. Recent work (e.g. on parabolic-hyperbolic formulations and on hyperboloidal data without logarithmic singularities, 2024–2025) further characterizes subclasses of asymptotic data yielding smooth or Bondi-regular development. A complete characterization of the optimal asymptotic conditions for the conformal method in this setting is not yet established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Generic asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets admit polyhomogeneous expansions, and only a non-generic subclass of solutions of the conformal constraint equations is free of logarithmic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Smoothness at infinity for conformal-method hyperboloidal data is non-generic; characterization is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: A Large Class of Non-Constant Mean Curvature Solutions of the Einstein Constraint Equations on an Asymptotically Hyperbolic Manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for solutions of the conformal constraint equations on asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds, including non-CMC cases.
status_evidence.claim: Existence theory under specified asymptotic conditions is partially developed.

status_evidence.title: At the interface of asymptotics, conformal methods and analysis in general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing conformal methods, asymptotic conditions, and outstanding issues for hyperboloidal data.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates open issues remain in characterizing asymptotic conditions.
